study type: Prospective cohort combined with retrospective cohort (observational)
exposure: Vaginal dinoprostone (prostaglandin E2) for cervical ripening
outcome: Favorable cervix (Bishop score >= 6) 24 hours after cervical ripening
Mean induction time to vaginal delivery
cohort: The study participants were 92 obese women (pre-pregnancy BMI > 30 kg/m2) at term (> 37 weeks) with live singleton fetuses in vertex presentation and an unfavorable cervix (Bishop score < 6), undergoing labor induction.
finding: A double-balloon catheter was significantly more efficient at achieving a favorable cervix (Bishop score >= 6) after 24 hours compared to vaginal dinoprostone in obese women at term.
mod_finding: No significant difference was observed in the cesarean section rate or the mean induction time to vaginal delivery between the double-balloon catheter and vaginal dinoprostone groups.
